 Barcelona's next superstar?  
 U17 World Cup: 124 starlets with market values and top ten wonderkids ranked 
 ©TM/IMAGO 
 The U17 World Cup gets underway in Qatar today with some of the best young talent in the world descending on the Middle East. Scouts from the major European clubs will be in attendance aiming to unearth the next wonderkid and plenty of relatively unknown gems are ready to make their name. Forty-eight nations will participate and they’ll be split into 12 groups of four, but the United States pulled out recently due to safety concerns.
 U17 World Cup 
 Homepage 
 Portugal are the reigning champions after lifting the trophy in 2025, while Nigeria are the most decorated nation after winning it five times. Victor Osimhen is the top scorer in the history of the U17 World Cup with ten goals while Cesc Fàbregas , Toni Kroos and Phil Foden have all been voted player of the tournament. In total, 124 players at this year’s competition already have market values on Transfermarkt and we’ve analysed the top ten most valuable players - you can view every starlet with a valuation below.
 U17 World 
 Every player with market value 
 U17 World Cup: Top ten most valuable stars
 Jorge Domínguez will be the most valuable star on show with the Atlético Madrid starlet already valued at €8m with Spain amongst the favourites to win the title. Barcelona have great hopes for Ebrima Tunkara as the next La Masia superstar and he’ll be vital to Spain’s prospects. Riccardo Cassano’s reputation skyrocketed recently after he was called up to the Italian national squad, despite not making his professional debut for Como.
 Interestingly, Holmes Júnior is the only player on the list not contracted to a first tier club with the defender at Girona in 2. LaLiga. Belgium has produced a conveyor belt of talent in recent years with Xander Dierckx and Elie Mbavu represented. Seven of the ten players listed are European with Argentina's Simón Escobar , Brazil’s Kauê Furquim and Ecuador’s Luis Fragozo joining them. We’ve closely examined five starlets we’re backing to become household names.
 U17 World Cup: Five starlets to watch
 Market Value 
 J. Domínguez 
 Centre-Back 
 € 8.00 M 
 As highlighted in our graphic, Spanish centre-back Jorge Domínguez is the most valuable player at the competition with a market value of €8m. Domínguez is also the ninth most valuable player in the world born in 2009 with Max Dowman leading the way at €50m. The defender became Atleti’s youngest ever debutant in LaLiga when he started against Malaga in August, aged 16 years and 241 days. Dominguez is extremely powerful already and he frequently dominates attackers at youth level. He’s also extremely quick and his long-stride allows him to cover large distances. Simeone has also played him at right-back but he’s expected to develop into a senior Spanish international at centre-back.
 Market Value 
 F. Croci 
 Second Striker 
 € 3.00 M 
 Federico Croci is one of only two players born in 2010 to be called up by head coach Manuel Pasqual, a testament to how quickly the Fiorentina forward has developed and how much experience he has already gained. He made his first-team debut in the Coppa Italia in August and announced himself on the European stage with a goal and a superb performance in a 5–0 UEFA Youth League win over Septemvri Sofia. That match showcased all his qualities. He timed his runs in behind the defence well, showed a burst of pace, dropped deep before darting forward again, and used his body intelligently to bring the ball under control and shield it. He also showed real tenacity. He could be just the explosive player Italy needs.
 Market Value 
 E. Tunkara 
 Attacking Midfield 
 € 5.00 M 
 Ebrima Tunkara was named MVP at the most recent Under-17 European Championship, even though Spain went out in the semi-finals. That was the only match in which he neither scored nor provided an assist. Before that setback, he had put up the numbers of a genuine star. He’s a No. 10 who orchestrates the attack and can finish moves himself. Some people even say that La Masia hasn’t seen a talent like him since Lamine Yamal emerged. He hasn’t made his first-team debut yet, but he has been named on the bench for two LaLiga games this season.
 Market Value 
 E. Mbavu 
 Centre-Back 
 € 3.00 M 
 Alongside Italy’s Ludovico Varali, Elie Mvabu was one of the two standout centre-backs at the 2026 Under-17 European Championship. Belgium conceded just twice with him on the pitch, including a last-gasp penalty that took the final to extra time and paved the way for an Italian victory. Already ready for professional football, he has made eight appearances for Genk’s under-21 side in Belgium’s second tier. He’s a commanding physical presence, vocal in organising his teammates, quick to get back and cover, and capable of breaking lines with powerful surges forward.
 Market Value 
 S. Escobar 
 Left-Back 
 € 4.00 M 
 Simon Escobar is a full-back who makes things happen. In defence, he has a good feel for when to go in and how to make the challenge. On the ball, he’s almost brazen. He keeps it close at full tilt, daring opponents to press before slipping through the gaps they leave. It always feels as though he’s one touch away from losing it, but when he gets clear, whether down the flank or through the middle, he gives his team an attacking outlet few full-backs can offer. He heads into the youth World Cup valued at €4 million, with plenty of time left on his contract at Vélez . Even so, there’s a strong sense that things could change fast, whatever Vélez might have to say about it.
